title: Pesticide applicator scope, definitions and effective dates practice questions
description: Practice questions on 40 CFR Part 171 Subpart A: scope, who is a certified applicator, key definitions and effective dates (171.1-171.5).

questions.question: Under 171.1(b), when is a person a certified applicator for purposes of FIFRA?

options.A: Once the person has completed a pesticide manufacturer's product training
options.B: Once the person has used restricted use pesticides under direct supervision for one season
options.C: Only if the person holds a certification issued pursuant to a plan approved in accordance with Part 171 and currently valid in the pertinent jurisdiction
options.D: Whenever the person holds a certification from any jurisdiction, even one that has expired

questions.explanation: 171.1(b): a person is a certified applicator "only if the person holds a certification issued pursuant to a plan approved in accordance with this part and currently valid in the pertinent jurisdiction."

questions.question: What does 171.1(b) say about making available for use, or using, a pesticide classified for restricted use other than in accordance with Part 171?

options.A: It is unlawful for any person, as provided in FIFRA section 12(a)(2)(F)
options.B: It is allowed if the person notifies EPA in writing beforehand
options.C: It is unlawful only for commercial applicators
options.D: It is allowed for private applicators on land they own

questions.explanation: 171.1(b): "As provided in FIFRA section 12(a)(2)(F), it is unlawful for any person to make available for use or to use any pesticide classified for restricted use other than in accordance with the requirements of this part."

questions.question: Besides certified applicators, whose use of restricted use pesticides do the Part 171 standards set requirements for, according to 171.1(a)?

options.A: Farmworkers entering fields after an application
options.B: Homeowners using general use pesticides at home
options.C: Workers at pesticide production plants
options.D: Noncertified persons using restricted use pesticides under the direct supervision of a certified applicator

questions.explanation: 171.1(a): the standards address "requirements for noncertified persons using restricted use pesticides under the direct supervision of a certified applicator."

questions.question: Under 171.3, "practical knowledge" means having the pertinent facts and comprehension sufficient to properly perform functions associated with use of restricted use pesticides. What does the definition say this includes?

options.A: Holding a college degree in a pest-related science
options.B: Properly responding to reasonably foreseeable problems and situations
options.C: Having at least one year of experience under direct supervision
options.D: Passing a performance test in every certification category

questions.explanation: 171.3: "Practical knowledge means the possession of pertinent facts and comprehension sufficient to properly perform functions associated with use of restricted use pesticides, including properly responding to reasonably foreseeable problems and situations."

questions.question: A worker who is not certified in the category appropriate to the application is mixing a restricted use pesticide under the direct supervision of a certified private applicator. What does 171.3 call this worker?

options.A: A restricted use pesticide retail dealer
options.B: A noncertified applicator
options.C: A certifying authority
options.D: A certified private applicator

questions.explanation: 171.3 defines a noncertified applicator as a person "who is not certified" in the appropriate category "but who is using restricted use pesticides under the direct supervision of a person certified as a commercial or private applicator in accordance with this part."

questions.question: A State agency issues restricted use pesticide applicator certifications under a certification plan approved by EPA. What does 171.3 call that agency?

options.A: A dealership
options.B: A noncertified applicator
options.C: An Indian Tribe
options.D: A certifying authority

questions.explanation: 171.3: "Certifying authority means the Agency, or a State, Tribal, or Federal agency that issues restricted use pesticide applicator certifications pursuant to a certification plan approved by the Agency under this part."

questions.question: Under 171.3, "certification" is a certifying authority's issuance of authorization to a person to do what?

options.A: Use or supervise the use of restricted use pesticides
options.B: Distribute or sell restricted use pesticides at a dealership
options.C: Register new pesticide products
options.D: Approve State certification plans

questions.explanation: 171.3: "Certification means a certifying authority's issuance, pursuant to this part, of authorization to a person to use or supervise the use of restricted use pesticides."

questions.question: According to the 171.3 definition of "competency", the nature and degree of competency required relate directly to what?

options.A: The number of years the applicator has held a certification
options.B: The number of employees in the applicator's business
options.C: The nature of the activity and the degree of independent responsibility
options.D: The applicator's age

questions.explanation: 171.3 says competency is required "where the nature and degree of competency required relate directly to the nature of the activity and the degree of independent responsibility."

questions.question: An applicator transports pesticide containers that have been opened. Under 171.3, this activity falls within which defined term?

options.A: Calibration
options.B: Compatibility
options.C: Use
options.D: Application

questions.explanation: 171.3 defines "Use" to include "Other pesticide-related activities, including, but not limited to, transporting or storing pesticide containers that have been opened". "Application" means "the dispersal of a pesticide" toward a target site.

questions.question: Under the 171.3 definition of "use", supervising the use of a pesticide by a noncertified applicator is included in which activity?

options.A: Applying the pesticide
options.B: Calibration of application equipment
options.C: Disposing of excess pesticides
options.D: Storing pesticide containers

questions.explanation: 171.3 lists "Applying the pesticide, including, but not limited to, supervising the use of a pesticide by a noncertified applicator."

questions.question: An applicator measures a sprayer's output and adjusts the sprayer to establish a specific rate of dispersal. Under the 171.3 definition of "calibration", what else does that adjustment establish, if applicable?

options.A: The pesticide's toxicity to nontarget organisms
options.B: The compatibility of the pesticide with other chemicals
options.C: The restricted entry interval for the treated area
options.D: Droplet or particle size of a pesticide, and/or an equalized dispersal pattern

questions.explanation: 171.3: "Calibration means measurement of dispersal or output of application equipment and adjustment of such equipment to establish a specific rate of dispersal and, if applicable, droplet or particle size of a pesticide, and/or equalized dispersal pattern."

questions.question: Under 171.3, what makes a pesticide a "fumigant"?

options.A: It is any pesticide applied inside an enclosed structure
options.B: It is a restricted use pesticide that bears labeling designating it as a fumigant
options.C: It is any pesticide sold at a dealership
options.D: It is any pesticide a State lists as highly toxic

questions.explanation: 171.3: "Fumigant means a restricted use pesticide that bears labeling designating it as a fumigant." Fumigation "means the use of a fumigant."

questions.question: A restricted use pesticide retail dealer owns a farm-supply store where it sells restricted use pesticides. What does 171.3 call that store?

options.A: A dealership
options.B: A certifying authority
options.C: A seed treatment facility
options.D: A pesticide production plant

questions.explanation: 171.3: "Dealership means any establishment owned or operated by a restricted use pesticide retail dealer where restricted use pesticides are distributed or sold."

questions.question: Which transactions does the 171.3 definition of "restricted use pesticide retail dealer" exclude?

options.A: Sales of restricted use pesticides to certified private applicators
options.B: Sales of restricted use pesticides to certified commercial applicators
options.C: Sales made from a location in Indian country
options.D: Transactions solely between persons who are pesticide producers, registrants, wholesalers, or retail sellers, acting only in those capacities

questions.explanation: A retail dealer is "any person who distributes or sells restricted use pesticides to any person, excluding transactions solely between persons who are pesticide producers, registrants, wholesalers, or retail sellers, acting only in those capacities."

questions.question: How does 171.3 define a "mishap"?

options.A: Only an unexpected event that injures the applicator
options.B: Only an intentional misuse of a restricted use pesticide
options.C: An event that adversely affects man or the environment and is related to the use or presence of a pesticide, whether the event was unexpected or intentional
options.D: Any spill at a dealership

questions.explanation: 171.3: "Mishap means an event that adversely affects man or the environment and that is related to the use or presence of a pesticide, whether the event was unexpected or intentional."

questions.question: A business applies restricted use pesticides in three States. What does the 171.3 definition of "principal place of business" say it may do?

options.A: It must use its headquarters office as its principal place of business for all three States
options.B: It may designate a location within each State as its principal place of business for that State
options.C: It must ask EPA to designate its principal place of business
options.D: It may use only an office, never a residence, as its principal place of business

questions.explanation: 171.3: a person who applies restricted use pesticides in more than one State "may designate a location within a State or area of Indian country as its principal place of business for that State or area of Indian country." The principal location may be "either residence or office".

questions.question: Under the 171.3 definition of "Indian country", which land within an Indian reservation under the jurisdiction of the United States Government is included?

options.A: All land within the limits of the reservation, notwithstanding the issuance of any patent, including rights-of-way running through the reservation
options.B: Only reservation land for which no patent has been issued
options.C: Reservation land, excluding rights-of-way running through it
options.D: Only land that a Tribe has designated as a principal place of business

questions.explanation: 171.3 includes "All land within the limits of any Indian reservation under the jurisdiction of the United States Government, notwithstanding the issuance of any patent, and, including rights-of-way running through the reservation."

questions.question: Under 171.5(a), on what date is Part 171 effective?

options.A: January 4, 2017
options.B: March 4, 2020
options.C: March 6, 2017
options.D: November 4, 2023

questions.explanation: 171.5(a): "This part is effective March 6, 2017."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.5, Effective date (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A certifying authority's plan was approved by EPA before March 6, 2017, and by March 4, 2020 it submitted a proposed modification. Under 171.5(c), until when does the earlier plan remain in effect (subject to paragraph (d) and 171.309(b))?

options.A: Until March 4, 2020, regardless of the submission
options.B: Until EPA approves the modified plan, with no end date
options.C: Until EPA approves or rejects the modified plan or November 4, 2023, whichever is later
options.D: Until EPA approves or rejects the modified plan or November 4, 2023, whichever is earlier

questions.explanation: 171.5(c): the earlier plan "will remain in effect until EPA has approved or rejected the modified plan pursuant to § 171.309(a)(4) or November 4, 2023, whichever is earlier", except as provided in paragraph (d) and 171.309(b).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.5, Effective date (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.5(e), when may a State, Tribe or Federal agency without an EPA-approved certification plan in effect submit a plan to EPA for review and approval?

options.A: Only before March 4, 2020
options.B: Any time, if the plan meets or exceeds all of the applicable requirements of Part 171
options.C: Only before November 4, 2023
options.D: Only after another jurisdiction's plan has been rejected

questions.explanation: 171.5(e): they "may submit to EPA for review and approval a certification plan that meets or exceeds all of the applicable requirements of this part any time."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.5, Effective date (as of Nov 4, 2026)
